answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a fixed bond before accepting paid work, with that bond forfeited when verifiable fraud is proved. Whether agents tend an orchard, supply an oasis, or monitor a glacier, the rule is the same: creating names is free, but activating 1,000 fake workers requires 1,000 bonds. The attacker must tie up capital for every usable identity and loses that capital on identities caught cheating.
